text: The converse of Lagrange's theorem holds in every finite group: if d divides |G|, then G has a subgroup of order d.
explanation: False. Lagrange guarantees only that a subgroup's order divides |G|, not the converse: A₄ has order 12 yet has no subgroup of order 6. So a divisor of |G| need not be realized as the order of a subgroup.
